thread:
incident-bot: paging on-call: latency SLO breach detected for /v1/chat/streaming — p95 and p99 spike observed across us-west-2 :rotating_light:

sara-dev: seeing big tail latency starting ~11:04 UTC, p95 jumped to ~1.2s and p99 to ~8.5s for streaming responses. a few customers reporting stalls while tokens are generating.

miguel-sre: @sara-dev can you attach the logs you already grabbed? any correlation with deploys?

sara-dev: no deploys in last 30m. rolling CPU increase on preproc workers, saw repeated GC + long syscalls in the tokenizer process. dumping a short snippet:```
[2026-03-14T11:07:02Z] preproc-worker-12 pid=2345 cpu=92% rss=1.6G
tokenizer: parse_time=0.013 ms tokens=40
tokenizer: parse_time=1.45 ms tokens=740  <-- big jump
stream-handler: stall=4500ms waiting on preproc
```

sara-dev: also attached profiling snapshot to the incident channel, but short term mitigation ideas: 1) flip prompt_json_mode off for affected routes, 2) fall back to legacy tokenizer, 3) route traffic to canary model variant without heavy schema validation.

oncall-bot: @miguel-sre you have been notified (priority: p1). See runbook: Tokenizer tail latency. Link: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/tokenizer-tail

miguel-sre: taking this one. quick note: recent prompt template change rolled 10:46 UTC by kevin-eng added extra tool-schema validation step that glues JSON parsing + regex for each tool param — could be hot path.

kevin-eng: yep that was my change to validate tool schemas on the fly for chat->tools. rolling back is easy (revert commit abc1234). should we revert immediately?

miguel-sre: yes please revert while we investigate. prioritize unblock over change correctness. @kevin-eng run:```
git revert abc1234 --no-edit
DEPLOY_TARGET=preproc-services ./deploy.sh --hotfix
```

kevin-eng: running revert now, will follow logs.

elaine-pm: alerting CS for impacted customers: will send blurb and severity. list of top customers: acme, finplug, docwrite.ai — they reported streaming stalls.

kevin-eng: revert completed, preproc services rolling. logs show fewer long regex runs after restart.

sara-dev: metrics after 90s: p95 down to ~380ms, p99 down to ~1.1s on affected routes. still watching for residuals and cache cold effects.

miguel-sre: good, but we need root cause. initial hypothesis: prompt_json_mode enabled a per-tool validation path that for certain nested schemas triggered a slow regex-based sanitizer; for large tool input sizes this turned O(n^2) and blocked worker threads.

kevin-eng: snippet of the problematic code we added:```python
# naive schema sanitizer
for field in fields:
    val = re.sub(r"[^\x00-\x7F]", "", field)  # <- expensive for long strings
    parsed = json.loads(val)
```

kevin-eng: switching to streamed json parsing + size checks and moving heavy validation off the fast path is the long term fix. will open PR after incident.

miguel-sre: immediate postmortem actions:
- revert landed and reduced impact (confirmed)
- create alert to watch preproc tokenization syscalls > 75% for 5m (assigned to eng-platform)
- add canary guard to prompt_json_mode rollout (feature flag + traffic threshold)
- update runbook: add checklist for tool-schema changes and perf tests

elaine-pm: CS action: notify affected customers with status, ETA for full fix ~24-48h, offer mitigation knobs (disable prompt_json_mode) via support ticket.

cs-triage-bot: created ticket RED-4531 for acme, RED-4532 for finplug, RED-4533 for docwrite.ai (owner: cs-team).

miguel-sre: handing off to @kevin-eng for remediation work + PR. I'll monitor overnight and reopen page if regressions.

kevin-eng: thanks — I'll add benchmarks to the PR and a micro-benchmark for long tool payloads. plan: implement streamed JSON parse, add pre-check max_tool_payload_chars, and move schema validation to async background worker.

sara-dev: quick note for dashboards: add a per-route breakdown that surfaces time spent in preproc.tokenizer and preproc.schema_validation so we can catch this earlier.

miguel-sre: agreed. also adding a temporary tag on metrics: "postfix:tokenizer-hotfix-1773501284" for easier query.

incident-bot: incident state: mitigated (paging cleared), root cause suspected: new on-path schema validation + regex sanitizer causing tokenizer CPU storms and tail latency. follow-up: postmortem scheduled 2026-03-15 16:00 UTC. Owners: kevin-eng (remediation), miguel-sre (post-incident ops), elaine-pm (customer comms).

kevin-eng: will send PR link and perf numbers once ready.

miguel-sre: handing off to night on-call @natalie-sre in 20m with notes and links. if anything flares, page p0.

natalie-sre: acknowledged, will standby. :thumbsup:

sara-dev: closing thread but keeping logs pinned for postmortem. thanks team. :clap:
